decisions.reason: Section 1 names fs-ext@2.1.1 as a pinned dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl (manifest-excerpt.json), shows its install script running node-gyp configure build, quotes the gyp ERR! find VS output from install-error.log, and attributes the failure to the missing MSVC toolchain rather than pnpm or network issues.

Section 2 uses lease-excerpt.md's top-level flock import, explains the loader must resolve fs-ext even on Windows before any branch, and concludes --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install time to module-load time, so the service still cannot boot.

Section 3 contrasts POSIX non-blocking flock(2) via fs-ext with Windows acquireLockHandleWin32's named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW bindings from win32-excerpt.ts), explains the flock binding is dead code on Windows, and the plan keeps real native flock on Linux/macOS while Windows locking stays on the semaphore (verification items 3-4).

Section 4 follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: a guarded install script that skips node-gyp on win32, a try/catch entry with a pure-JS flock(fd, op, cb) fallback that warns once and invokes the callback, registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml including allowBuilds, plus reinstall, require('fs-ext') load, dsh web --no-open HTTP 200, and POSIX-native verification checks and a rollback path.

The plan explicitly states no Visual Studio will be installed (owner constraint) and no upstream fork, version bump, or hand-edit; the fix stays within the repository-managed pnpm patch, which the report notes is applied declaratively at install time.

Section 5 cites the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and connects it throughout to the fs-ext install failure and the Windows pnpm-patch recipe, tying sections 1-4 to the card's symptoms and migration steps.

caps.reason: The plan affirmatively forbids installing Visual Studio or Build Tools; MSVC is only described as the missing toolchain causing the failure.
The report rejects --ignore-scripts as insufficient (section 2) and the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via the pure-JS fallback, not merely skipping the build.
The plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism and explicitly rules out forking, version bumps, or upstream edits.

Windows locking remains on the named semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock; the warn-once no-op fallback exists only so the import resolves on Windows and is flagged as a visible signal, not a universal lock bypass.
